clue.text: Not here to look after man who is preoccupied

parts.note: someone not here is absent
to mind children is to look after them
Ed is a common man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A man who looks after something is too preoccupied to be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in thought, with attention elsewhere, is forgetful in the way the phrase describes.

clue.text: Do their deals leave them more impoverished by Sunday?

definitions.text: Do their deals leave them more impoverished by Sunday?

parts.note: broke means penniless, so more broke means more impoverished

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether dealers end the week poorer for their trading.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: these dealers might indeed be poorer after their deals, and the wordplay puts S after the comparative of 'broke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockbrokers and other agents make deals for clients, and the question teases that dealing could leave them out of pocket.

clue.text: Turn and sneer when trapped

indicators.note: to turn something over is to churn it up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a trap turns and sneers at their captor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' rearranges the letters of AND and SNEER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in a snare or net is a synonym of being trapped.

clue.text: Time to do it yourself? Initially disorderly, becoming neat

indicators.note: the initial letters of the phrase are put into disorder, so they are rearranged

parts.note: do it yourself is shortened to its initials, DIY, home improvement work

explanation.surface: Time for some home improvement: messy at first, but the place ends up neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' tells you to use the initials of 'do it yourself', and 'disorderly' scrambles them; 'becoming' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orderly and well kept is a synonym of neat.

clue.text: It's rude to point at the Spanish prisoner

indicators.note: the Spanish article is held captive, a prisoner inside the verb

parts.note: to indicate something is to point at it
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Pointing at a Spanish prisoner is a rude thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coarse or lacking in tact is a synonym of rude.

clue.text: Fear the padre advised repatriation for some

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run found inside them

explanation.surface: A priest's suggestion that some people go home causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some' signals a run of letters across 'padre advised'; 'repatriation' adds to the picture of a priest's advice but gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror or great apprehension is a synonym of fear.

clue.text: No new dressing prepared for stray

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made up, so the letters are made up afresh
no means the named letter is left out

explanation.surface: No fresh dressing has been made ready for an animal that wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No new' removes N from DRESSING, leaving DRESSIG, and 'prepared' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander from the subject in talk is a synonym of stray.

clue.text: Studying the main subject scientifically

parts.note: the main is the sea in poetry, so this is about the scientific study of the seas

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, not the principal subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the science of the oceans, their currents and depths, fits a scientific study of the sea.

clue.text: In river, new mishaps dam aged movement of cargo

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands

indicators.note: read as one word, damaged signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Accidents on a river damage a dam and disrupt the moving of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam aged' is to be read as one word, 'damaged', the anagram signal; the surface splits it to suggest a broken dam.
explanation.definitionFit: Transferring freight from one vessel to another is a kind of movement of cargo.

clue.text: Sent the ball to the other side where Shearer headed inside and scored wildly

definitions.text: Sent the ball to the other side

indicators.note: inside means the footballer's first letter goes within the other letters
something done wildly is out of control, so the letters are scrambled
headed means only the leading letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: A football match report: Alan Shearer heads the ball and scores in a wild finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England centre forward. 'headed' takes his S and puts it inside the anagram of SCORED, signalled by 'wildly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, passing the ball across the pitch from the wing is a cross.

clue.text: It drags the doctor to the bank of the river

parts.note: the edge of something is its bank or border

explanation.surface: Something drags a doctor to the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that scrapes mud from the bottom of a harbour hauls a scoop along the bed.

clue.text: A near disaster at scene of battle

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A near disaster happens on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or field of conflict is where a fight takes place.

clue.text: Hit, but gore, we hear, has gone away

annotationWithheld.why: Hit, but gore, we hear, has gone away (8): BLOOD GONE said aloud gives BLUDGEON, but the spoken words 'gore' and 'has gone away' stand on either side of 'we hear', so no single leaf can hold the phrase heard, and one indicator cannot serve two sound() steps
annotationWithheld.clue: Hit, but gore, we hear, has gone away

clue.text: Where you are closely questioned on your taste for steak?

definitions.text: Where you are closely questioned on your taste for steak?

parts.words: Where you are closely questioned on your taste for steak?
parts.note: to grill someone is to question them hard, and a steak may be grilled, so this is a restaurant where food is cooked that way

explanation.walkthrough: 'closely questioned' points to grilling as an interrogation, but the place is a restaurant serving grilled meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants that specialise in grilled meats are places to eat steak.

clue.text: Taking care of other people's deliveries

definitions.text: Taking care of other people's deliveries

parts.words: Taking care of other people's deliveries
parts.note: the deliveries are births, not parcels, and this is the branch of medicine that handles them

explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests post or couriers, but here it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical specialty of pregnancy and childbirth looks after mothers giving birth.

clue.text: Sues over employment practices

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are turned over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker sues over the way staff are treated at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ways of employing something, or customary ways of doing things, are synonyms of practices.

clue.text: Healer needs to include temperature after the French produce a don

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the French article

parts.note: le is a French word for the

indicators.note: needs to include means the healer's word must take in the temperature

parts.note: one who cures is a healer

explanation.surface: A doctor must take a temperature after a French one helps produce an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge, is called a don.

clue.text: Game member was back

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union, the game
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A player in a game was back on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: The hindquarters or rear end of an animal is its back part.

clue.text: It's unfortunate if camel is doing mischief

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is an unlucky jumble, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: It's bad luck when a camel starts causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent and harmful, causing evil, describes something doing mischief.

clue.text: Soldier collects rubbish at centre of society notables

indicators.note: collects means the soldier gathers the other pieces inside himself

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
litter is rubbish dropped in the street

explanation.surface: A soldier picks up rubbish in the middle of a fashionable gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' only serves the surface; 'society notables' is the definition, not 'society' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable celebrities, the glamorous elite, are society's notables.

clue.text: Mean the Authorised Ver sion would upset 23?

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for the Authorised Version, the King James Bible

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: 23 refers to the answer of the clue at 23 down

explanation.surface: A question of whether the King James Bible would disturb something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorised Version is the 1611 King James translation of the Bible; '23' points to the answer at 23 down, which 'upset' scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic middle value.

clue.text: Large pal destroyed by wasting disease

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A big friend is killed off by a disease that wastes the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A niacin deficiency illness causing skin lesions and decline is a wasting disease.

clue.text: Engineers in time will come to the same conclusion

indicators.note: in means the engineers are placed within the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Given time, the engineers will reach the same verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur, sharing one view, is to reach the same conclusion.

clue.text: Run into them at the bathing establishment

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into acquaintances at the public baths.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spring or public bath in ancient Rome was a place for bathing.

clue.text: He won't go out with his mates for a crust

definitions.text: He won't go out with his mates
definitions.meaning: a strikebreaker keeps working when colleagues walk out
the dry crust that forms over a healing wound

explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker is called by this insult, and the same word names the hard covering on a healing cut.

clue.text: Get the impression New Orleans was hell

parts.note: to infer is to deduce or get an impression

explanation.surface: Someone senses that New Orleans was a hellish place.
explanation.definitionFit: A raging fire or place of torment is a picture of hell, as in Dante.

clue.text: Close of play

parts.note: a play is a theatre performance, and its end is marked by something coming down on stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Close of play' sounds like the end of a cricket day, but the play is a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The drape lowered at the end of a theatre performance marks its finish.

clue.text: Beg her rescuer right away to provide food -fast!

indicators.note: provide means the remaining letters are used to make up a fresh word
away means the named letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A woman begs her rescuer to get rid of something and bring food quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' drops one R from BEG HER RESCUER; the twelve letters left are rearranged. 'food -fast!' is fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilled beef patty in a bun is a staple of fast-food chains.
